chunks: In equating you with the Lord of all the worlds;
ai.seo_question: What did the poets claim about equating the Prophet with the Lord of the worlds?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse critiques the poets' claim to divine inspiration by contrasting their empty rhetoric with the Prophet's clear, miraculous signs. Shia exegesis often highlights how this verse underscores the Prophet's distinct status as a human messenger chosen by God, rather than a deity himself, refuting the 'deification' implied by the poets' boastful assertions. This serves as a theological boundary marker, affirming the Prophet's humanity while validating his prophethood through divine authority.
